speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are an 8-month-old boy having trouble with feeding and your belly looks swollen. Can you tell me exactly how long you have been having these problems, and is your vomit green or does it look like oil?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Intussusception. The combination of an 8-month-old infant with abdominal distension, feeding difficulties, and severe pain upon palpation (crying when the belly is touched) is highly suggestive of this condition, even in the absence of classic "currant jelly" stools or bilious vomiting at this specific moment.
